meta: You told AI to keep it short and fun, but after a while it forgot everything? This video uses the picture of a desk: AI's context has a limit, and old sheets fall off. Two tips to fix it.
prompt: Sum up our requests and decisions so far in 5 points

muc.title: Why does AI "forget" in long chats?
muc.text: At the start you told AI to keep it short and fun. After a while, it's writing long and serious. It forgot.

muc.title: AI works on a desk
muc.text: Picture AI working at a desk. Every message, yours or its own, is a sheet of paper on the desk. This desk is called the context.

muc.title: The desk has a limit
muc.text: No matter how big the desk is, it has a limit. When it's full, the oldest sheets get pushed off, or get buried in the pile, and AI stops noticing them.

muc.title: New chat = empty desk
muc.text: And when you start a new chat, the desk is empty. AI remembers nothing from last time, unless the app has a memory feature turned on.

muc.title: Summarize, then move to a new desk
muc.text: Tip one: if a chat gets too long, ask AI to sum up what you've agreed on, then paste that summary into a new chat.

muc.title: Repeat what matters
muc.text: Tip two: if a request is important, repeat it briefly in your new message.

muc.title: Sum it up in 5 points, then start fresh
muc.text: When a chat gets too long, type "sum up our requests in five points", then start over with that summary.
